'''Omari Johnson''' (born November 26, 1989) is a [[Jamaicans|Jamaican]] professional [[basketball]] player. Johnson played [[college basketball]] with the [[Oregon State Beavers men's basketball|Oregon State Beavers]] and graduated from high school at [[Susan Miller Dorsey High School]] in He has played professional basketball in the [[NBA]], the [[NBA G League]], Canada and Spain.

==High school career==
Johnson played high school basketball for [[Susan Miller Dorsey High School|Dorsey High School]] in Los Angeles.<ref name="bio">{{cite web|title=Omari Johnson Biography|url=http://www.osubeavers.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=207930653|website=OSUBeavers.com|access-date=31 May 2015|archive-date=September 24, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924062352/http://www.osubeavers.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=207930653|url-status=dead}}</ref> In his junior season, he came off the bench and averaged 11 points and 7 rebounds per game.<ref name="bio" /> As a senior, he averaged 18.3 points, 10.1 rebounds and 1.5 blocks per game, being named to the All-[[CIF Los Angeles City Section|CIF LA]] first team.<ref name="bio" /> Led by Johnson, Dorsey reached the sectional semifinals of CIF LA.<ref name="bio" />

==College career==
[[File:Omari Johnson.jpg|thumb|left|100px|alt=Omari Johnson playing for the Oregon State Beavers|Omari Johnson playing for Oregon State]]
After considering offers from [[Wyoming Cowboys basketball|Wyoming]], [[South Florida Bulls men's basketball|South Florida]], and [[Long Beach State Beach men's basketball|Long Beach State]], Johnson verbally committed to [[Oregon State Beavers men's basketball|Oregon State]] in [[Corvallis, Oregon|Corvallis]].<ref name="committ">{{cite web | url=http://www.scout.com/college/basketball/recruiting/story/572163-omari-johnson-reaches-decision | title=Omari Johnson Reaches Decision | publisher=Scout.com | date=September 24, 2006 | access-date=August 19, 2015 | author=Hicks, Greg}}</ref> He said his reason for choosing to go to [[Oregon State University]] was that Corvallis is a [[college town]] and he felt needed by his prospective teammates. Additionally he liked having the opportunity to compete against top talent in the [[Pac-10]].<ref name="bio" /><ref name="committ" /> He achieved a career-high performance in scoring with 19 points as a freshman, as the Beavers lost 76–63 to [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]].<ref name="bio" /><ref>{{cite news | url=http://tucson.com/sports/basketball/college/wildcats/final-arizona-oregon-state/article_65295954-feb8-5a95-ac07-6e0def065e60.html | title=Final: Arizona 76, Oregon State 63 | newspaper=Arizona Daily Star | date=January 3, 2008 | access-date=August 19, 2015 | author=Pascoe, Bruce}}</ref> He tied that feature as a sophomore, also recording his first double-double, with 10 rebounds, helping his team get past [[Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball|Nebraska]] with a narrow 64–63 win.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://journalstar.com/sports/huskers/mens-basketball/late-free-throws-get-oregon-state-past-nebraska/article_db6e3424-b51c-558a-807c-f16587ba54a6.html | title=Late free throws get Oregon State past Nebraska | publisher=Lincoln Journal Star | date=December 13, 2008 | access-date=August 19, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.osubeavers.com/fls/30800/old_site/pdf/m-baskbl/Johnson09Game-by-Game.pdf?DB_OEM_ID=30800 | title=2008–09 Oregon State basketball individual statistics Omari Johnson | publisher=Oregon State Athletics | access-date=August 19, 2015 | archive-date=September 24, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924075515/http://www.osubeavers.com/fls/30800/old_site/pdf/m-baskbl/Johnson09Game-by-Game.pdf?DB_OEM_ID=30800 | url-status=dead }}</ref>

Although 6-foot-7 when he started college, Johnson grew more than two inches before his junior season to reach a height of 6-foot-9.<ref>{{cite news | url=http://blog.oregonlive.com/behindbeaversbeat/2007/04/osu_hoops_signs_point_guard_ri.html | title=OSU hoops signs point guard Rickey Claitt, assistant Jeff Reinert is leaving program | newspaper=The Oregonian | date=April 16, 2007 | access-date=August 19, 2015 | author=Buker, Paul}}</ref><ref>{{cite news | url=http://www.gazettetimes.com/sports/beavers-sports/article_6729cdf4-fbee-11de-b312-001cc4c002e0.html | title=Johnson's game is growing | newspaper=Corvallis Gazette-Times | date=January 7, 2010 | access-date=August 19, 2015 | author=Hampton, Kevin}}</ref> Coach [[Craig Robinson (basketball)|Craig Robinson]] expected Johnson to become Oregon State's focal point in offense, but was mainly used as a reserve player due to his sub-par effort on the defensive end.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://blog.oregonlive.com/behindbeaversbeat/2010/02/oregon_states_omari_johnson_co.html |title=Oregon State's Omari Johnson could be a much-needed zone buster at Arizona State |last=Buker |first=Paul |newspaper=[[The Oregonian]] |publication-date=February 9, 2010}}</ref> Johnson had a breakout game in the 2010 [[Civil War (college rivalry)|Civil War rivalry game]] versus the [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon Ducks]], scoring a season-high 18 points on 4-of-6 three-pointers.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://blog.oregonlive.com/behindbeaversbeat/2010/02/oregon_state_62_oregon_42_beav.html |title=Oregon State 62, Oregon 42: Beavers get program's first sweep of Ducks in 17 years |last=Buker |first=Paul |newspaper=[[The Oregonian]] |publication-date=February 6, 2010}}</ref>

In his senior season Johnson achieved a career-high with 13 rebounds, also adding 15 points for his second career double-double, as Oregon State lost 83–80 to [[Seattle Redhawks men's basketball|Seattle]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.osubeavers.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=750187&SPID=127160&DB_OEM_ID=30800&ATCLID=207865335 | title=Oregon State at Seattle University – Oregon State Post-Game Quotes | publisher=Oregon State Athletics | date=November 18, 2010 | access-date=August 19, 2015 | archive-date=September 24, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924062758/http://www.osubeavers.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=750187&SPID=127160&DB_OEM_ID=30800&ATCLID=207865335 | url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite news | url=http://blog.oregonlive.com/behindbeaversbeat/2010/11/seattle_83_oregon_state_80_tur.html | title=Seattle 83, Oregon State 80: Turnovers, misses cost Beavers in second half | newspaper=The Oregonian | date=November 17, 2010 | access-date=August 19, 2015}}</ref> A few days later, he had a career-high 6 steals and added 13 points, as Oregon State lost 66–60 to [[Texas Southern Tigers basketball|Texas Southern]].<ref name="bio" /><ref>{{cite news | url=http://blog.oregonlive.com/behindbeaversbeat/2010/11/oregon_state_mens_basketball_t.html | title=Oregon State men's basketball team still learning how to win, and a 66–60 loss to Texas Southern is proof | newspaper=The Oregonian | date=November 21, 2010 | access-date=August 19, 2015 | author=Schnell, Lindsay}}</ref> Prior to the game against local rivals Oregon, Johnson said that his opponents were "a feisty little bunch of dudes...<ref name="oregonian">{{cite news | url=http://blog.oregonlive.com/behindbeaversbeat/2011/01/the_basketball_civil_war_beave.html | title=The basketball Civil War: Beavers' Omari Johnson calls the Ducks, 'a feisty little bunch of dudes' | newspaper=The Oregonian | date=January 18, 2011 | access-date=August 19, 2015 | author=Buker, Paul}}</ref> They bump us more, you get elbows in the back a little more than other games, it's just physically and verbally more intense." He added, "I wouldn't call 'em dirty".<ref name="oregonian" /> In four seasons with the Beavers, Johnson appeared in 120 games, starting 67 of them and averaged 6.4 [[points per game|points]] and 4.0 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.osubeavers.com/fls/30800/old_site/pdf/m-baskbl/OmariJohnsonStats.pdf?DB_OEM_ID=30800 | title=Omari Johnson Individual career history | publisher=Oregon State Athletics | access-date=August 19, 2015 | archive-date=September 24, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924075517/http://www.osubeavers.com/fls/30800/old_site/pdf/m-baskbl/OmariJohnsonStats.pdf?DB_OEM_ID=30800 | url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Oshawa Power (2011–2012)===
After graduating from college, Johnson was selected by the [[Oshawa Power]] to play in their 2011 pre-season squad.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.oyetimes.com/sports/basketball/14677-oshawa-power-roster-for-game-vs-london-lightning | title=Oshawa Power Roster for game vs. London Lightning | publisher=Oye! Times | date=October 24, 2011 | access-date=August 19, 2015 | author=Ebanks, Drew}}</ref> He played in Oshawa's inaugural game in the [[National Basketball League of Canada|NBL Canada]], posting 8 points and 3 rebounds.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.oyetimes.com/sports/basketball/14941-oshawa-power-fall-to-the-quebec-kebs-104-101 | title=Oshawa Power fall to the Quebec Kebs 104–101 | publisher=Oye! Times | date=October 31, 2011 | access-date=19 August 2015 | author=Ebanks, Drew}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.fiba2006.fiba.com/pages/eng/fc/gamecent/p/gid/2/grid/RS/rid/6000777/boxscore.html | title=Boxscores: Quebec Kebekwa–Oshawa Power 104–101 | publisher=FIBA | access-date=August 19, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150926201058/http://www.fiba2006.fiba.com/pages/eng/fc/gamecent/p/gid/2/grid/RS/rid/6000777/boxscore.html | archive-date=September 26, 2015 | url-status=dead }}</ref> Against the [[Halifax Rainmen]] he finished with career-highs in both scoring and rebounding with 37 and 16 respectively; his scoring performance being a then NBL Canada record.<ref name="record">{{cite web | url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=4338608 | title=Power Lose 117–93 to Halifax Rainmen | publisher=Our Sports Central | date=January 5, 2012 | access-date=August 19, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://thechronicleherald.ca/sports/49248-rainmen-make-it-nine-straight | title=Rainmen make it nine straight | publisher=The Chronicle Herald | date=January 6, 2012 | access-date=August 19, 2015 | author=Freeman, Brian}}</ref> In the wake of the loss Johnson commented: "We weren't guarding at all and had too many turnovers".<ref name="record" /> In the [[2012 NBA Development League Draft|D-League 2012 draft]], Johnson was selected 74th overall by the [[Canton Charge]], only to be waived a few days later.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.cantonrep.com/article/20121103/News/311039912 | title=Canton Charge 2012 NBA D-League Draft picks | publisher=The Repository | date=November 3, 2012 | access-date=August 22, 2015 | author=Weir, Josh}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/canton/news/charge_waive_three_2012_11_21.html | title=Charge Waive Three | publisher=Canton Charge | date=November 21, 2012 | access-date=August 22, 2015}}</ref>

===Summerside Storm (2012–2013)===
After being named in the [[All-NBL Canada Team|All-NBL Canada second-team]] and an [[List of NBL Canada All-Stars|All-Star]] in the [[2011–12 NBL Canada season|2011–12 season]], Johnson signed with the [[Island Storm|Summerside Storm]] in December 2012.<ref name="realgm">{{cite web|title=Omari Johnson Player Profile|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Omari-Johnson/Summary/6809|website=[[RealGM]]|access-date=31 May 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.journalpioneer.com/Sports/2012-12-24/article-3146902/Storm-adds-Omari-Johnson/1 | title=Storm adds Omari Johnson | publisher=The Journal Pioneer | date=December 24, 2012 | access-date=August 19, 2015}}</ref> He posted a season-high 34 points, along with 13 rebounds, to help the Storm overcome his former team, the Oshawa Power.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.theguardian.pe.ca/Sports/2013-03-08/article-3196557/Summerside-Storm-clinches-division-title-in-NBL-of-Canada/1 | title=Summerside Storm clinches division title in NBL of Canada | publisher=The Guardian (Charlottetown) | date=March 8, 2013 | access-date=August 20, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.fiba2006.fiba.com/pages/eng/fc/gameCent/p/leagueid//ot//pid/6057997/season/2013/tid/6004601/tidstat//playerView.html | title=Omari Johnson Season 2012/13 | publisher=FIBA | access-date=August 20, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924012329/http://www.fiba2006.fiba.com/pages/eng/fc/gameCent/p/leagueid//ot//pid/6057997/season/2013/tid/6004601/tidstat//playerView.html | archive-date=September 24, 2015 | url-status=dead }}</ref> During two seasons in [[Canada]], Johnson began 43 of his 57 regular-season games, averaging 18.5 points, 8.5 rebounds, 2.6 assists, 1.4 blocks and 1.4 steals per game.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nblcanada.com/nblcanada/images/NBL_Canada_2013-14_Pre-Season_Guide.pdf | title=NBL Canada 2013–14 Pre-Season Guide | publisher=NBL Canada | access-date=August 27, 2015}}</ref>

===CB Valladolid (2013–2014)===
In September 2013, Johnson signed with [[CB Valladolid]], an [[Liga ACB|ACB]] team.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://baloncesto.as.com/baloncesto/2013/09/30/acb/1380556866_478086.html | title=El Valladolid se refuerza con el jamaicano Omari Johnson | publisher=as | date=September 30, 2013 | access-date=July 27, 2015|language=es}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=97698 | title=Omari Johnson, décimo jugador del CB Valladolid | publisher=Liga ACB | date=September 30, 2013 | access-date=July 27, 2015 | language=es | archive-date=September 26, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150926235321/http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=97698 | url-status=dead }}</ref> In Spain, Johnson had his best scoring performance against [[FC Barcelona Baloncesto]], scoring a game-high 20 points.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.mundodeportivo.com/20131215/baloncesto/otros/109-50-el-barca-consigue-la-victoria-mas-abultada-de-la-historia-de-la-acb_54396224309.html | title=109–50. El Barça consigue la victoria más abultada de la historia de la ACB | publisher=Mundo Deportivo | date=December 15, 2013 | access-date=August 22, 2015 | language=es}}</ref> Johnson started 24 of the season's 34 games, averaging 11.6 points and 6 rebounds per game in 26 minutes playing time.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.acb.com/stsacumjug.php?cod_jugador=H46 | title=Omari Johnson 2013–14 | publisher=Liga ACB | access-date=August 22, 2015 | language=es | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171114040635/http://www.acb.com/stsacumjug.php?cod_jugador=H46 | archive-date=November 14, 2017 | url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Maine Red Claws (2014–2016)===
Johnson was selected 39th overall in the [[2014 NBA Development League Draft|2014 NBA D-League Draft]] by the [[Maine Red Claws]].<ref>{{cite news | url=http://www.oregonlive.com/nba/index.ssf/2014/11/ex-trail_blazers_guard_elliot.html | title=Ex-Trail Blazers guard Elliot Williams is No. 2 pick in D-League draft | newspaper=The Oregonian | date=November 3, 2014 | access-date=July 27, 2015 | author=Tokito, Mike}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/draft2014/results.html | title=2014 NBA D-League Draft Board | publisher=NBA | access-date=July 27, 2015 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160504044400/http://www.nba.com/dleague/draft2014/results.html | archive-date=May 4, 2016 }}</ref> In February 2015, playing against the [[Westchester Knicks]], he had a season-high performance of 30 points, also having 15 rebounds.<ref>{{cite news | url=http://www.pressherald.com/2015/02/07/red-claws-cruise-past-westchester-121-108/ | title=Red Claws cruise past Westchester, 121–108 | newspaper=Portland Press Herald | date=February 7, 2015 | access-date=August 22, 2015 | author=Jordan, Glenn}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://stats.nbadleague.com/playerGameLogs.html?PlayerID=204179&pageNo=1&rowsPerPage=25&sortField=PTS&sortOrder=DES | title=Omari Johnson 2014–15 Game Log | publisher=D-League | access-date=August 22, 2015}}</ref> He tied his scoring season-high two weeks later, against the same opponent, grabbing 14 rebounds to achieve a double-double.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.lohud.com/story/sports/nba/knicks/2015/02/21/westchester-knicks-give-pomonas-jr-inman-second-shot/23820613/ | title=Westchester Knicks give Pomona's JR Inman a second shot | publisher=The Journal News | date=February 21, 2015 | access-date=August 22, 2015 | author=Zacchio, Mike}}</ref> On September 25, 2015, Johnson signed with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-announce-2015-training-camp-roster-presented-ohsu|title=Trail Blazers Announce 2015 Training Camp Roster, Presented by OHSU|work=NBA.com|date=September 25, 2015|access-date=September 25, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://blogs.columbian.com/blazer-banter/2015/09/25/trail-blazers-release-training-camp-roster-add-omari-johnson-for-camp/|title=Trail Blazers release Training Camp roster, add Omari Johnson for camp|work=The Columbian Blogs|date=September 25, 2015|access-date=September 25, 2015}}</ref> However, on October 23, he was waived after appearing in four preseason games.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-waive-pressey-and-johnson|title=Trail Blazers Waive Pressey and Johnson|work=NBA.com|date=October 23, 2015|access-date=October 23, 2015}}</ref> On October 31, he was reacquired by the Red Claws.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=5065518|title=Red Claws Announce Draft Results, Training Camp Roster|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=October 31, 2015|access-date=October 31, 2015}}</ref>

===Neptūnas Klaipėda (2016–2017)===
On November 9, 2016, Johnson signed with [[BC Neptūnas|Neptūnas Klaipėda]] of the [[Lietuvos krepšinio lyga|Lithuanian League]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.eurobasket.com/Lithuania/news/468848/Neptunas-sign-Omari-Johnson|title=Neptunas sign Omari Johnson|work=Eurobasket.com|date=November 9, 2016|access-date=November 20, 2016}}</ref> On February 10, 2017, he parted ways with Neptūnas due to disciplinary issues.<ref>{{cite news|title=DĖL VIDAUS TAISYKLIŲ PAŽEIDIMŲ "NEPTŪNĄ" PALIEKA DU LEGIONIERIAI|url=http://www.bcneptunas.lt/lt/titulinis/item/1381-dėl-vidaus-taisyklių-pažeidimų-"neptūną"-palieka-du-legionieriai|access-date=February 10, 2017|work=bcneptunas.lt|date=February 10, 2017|language=lt}}{{Dead link|date=April 2020 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last1=Miknevičiūtė|first1=Gabrielė|title=Iš "Neptūno" išmestas O.Kurauskas nesigaili priimtų sprendimų ir atskleidė D.Ewingo sugrįžimo istoriją {{!}} Krepsinis.net|url=http://www.krepsinis.net/naujiena/is-neptuno-ismestas-o-kurauskas-nesigaili-priimtu-sprendimu-ir-atskleide-d-ewingo-sugrizimo-istorija/273227|website=Krepsinis.net|access-date=25 April 2017|language=lt}}</ref>

===Memphis Hustle (2017–2018)===
On August 23, 2017, Johnson was selected by the [[Memphis Hustle]] in the NBA G League expansion draft.<ref>{{cite news|title=2017 NBA G League Expansion Draft Results|url=http://gleague.nba.com/news/2017-nba-g-league-expansion-draft-results/|access-date=August 23, 2017|work=NBA.com|date=August 23, 2017}}</ref>

===Memphis Grizzlies (2018)===
On April 6, 2018, the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] announced they had signed Johnson to multi-year contract.<ref>{{cite news|title=Memphis Grizzlies sign Omari Johnson to multi-year contract|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-sign-omari-johnson-to-multi-year-contract-180406|date=April 6, 2018|work=NBA.com|access-date=April 6, 2018}}</ref> He would make his NBA debut before the end of the 2017–18 season. On June 24, 2018, he was released by the Memphis Grizzlies.

=== Fort Wayne Mad Ants (2018–2019)===
On September 21, 2018, Johnson signed with the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref name="Pacers-Training-Camp">{{cite web |title=Pacers Announce 2018 Training Camp Roster |url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-announce-2018-training-camp-roster |website=NBA.com |access-date=September 21, 2018 |date=September 21, 2018}}</ref> He was waived on October 11, 2018, by Indiana. He played in 2018 and 2019 for the Fort Wayne Mad Ants (the G-League affiliate of the Indiana Pacers) who acquired his G-league rights in a trade with the Memphis Hustle(Memphis Grizzlies G-League team). He was added to the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]] training camp roster.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Cohn |first1=Justin |title=Ants announce roster as camp set to open |url=http://www.journalgazette.net/sports/professional/madants/20181022/ants-announce-roster-as-camp-set-to-open |access-date=October 22, 2018 |work=[[The Journal Gazette]] |date=October 22, 2018 |archive-date=November 23, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211123054853/https://www.journalgazette.net/sports/professional/madants/20181022/ants-announce-roster-as-camp-set-to-open |url-status=dead }}</ref> On February 23, 2019, Johnson recorded a career-high 8 3-pointers as he recorded 28 points, 6 rebounds and 2 assists in a 99–100 losing effort to the Canton Charge.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://stats.gleague.nba.com/game/2021800499/|title=Canton Charge 100 Fort Wayne Mad Ants 99|publisher=NBA G-League Stats|date=February 23, 2019|access-date=September 28, 2019}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Omari Johnson is the son of Jennifer Gordon and Dave Johnson. He hails from [[Kingston, Jamaica]]. Both of his parents are former basketball players, his mother at [[Florida Tech Panthers|Florida Tech]] in [[Melbourne, Florida|Melbourne]], and his father at [[Shaw University]] in [[Raleigh, North Carolina]]. He has two brothers, Shakir and Kahlil.<ref name="bio" />
